newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: GOLF-LIGHTNING CURTAILS SECOND ROUND OF OPEN.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-LIGHTNING CURTAILS SECOND ROUND OF OPEN.

text.p: Denmark's Thomas Bjorn and local player Wayne Bradley shared the lead when persistent lightning left the second round of the South African Open unfinished on Friday.
Bjorn, last year's European Tour rookie of the year, compiled an excellent 69 while Bradley, the first-round leader after a 65, added a 70.
They will approach the weekend differently.
The Dane just missed out on automatic selection for Europe's last Ryder Cup team and seems calmly determined to make the best of his excellent start:
"I will not change anything, not try to get clever. This is an excellent golf course and it deserves espect."
For Bradley, 31-year-old winner of just two minor tournaments in his career but a hugely gifted ball striker, the problem will be nerves.
"I know I must concentrate on my own game but you can't help thinking about the big names breathing down your neck. I've just got to try and keep my nerves and emotions in check," he said.
Veteran Irishman Eamonn Darcy, 44, is poised to challenge for the lead having turned in 33 to stand just a shot behind the leaders with eight holes to complete at first light on Saturday.

Defending champion Ernie Els seemed about to take the tournament by the scruff of the neck when he birdied the third and eagled the sixth to move into the lead at nine under par. But three consecutive bogeys around the turn dropped him into a five-way tie at six under.
He is one of 77 players still to finish their rounds.

Former world number one Nick Price also moved into contention with a round of 66 that made up for a disappointing 72 on the first day. Price did not drop a shot all day while two of his six birdies came with curling putts of 15 feet at two of the par hrees.

Fellow Zimbabwean Mark McNulty, a three times winner on the South African tour so far, posted a second consecutive 69 to draw level with Price and seems to have regained his very best touch around the greens with several tricky birdie putts as well as three excellent up-and-down saves for par.

England's David Gilford and Fijian Vijay Singh have also begun to mount challenges with bogey-free halfway loops of 33 to move to six under par with eight and nine holes to complete of the second round.
